mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong immediate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: Hong Kong Companies Registry certifies the certificate, then the High Court of Hong Kong Apostille Section affixes an apostille. No consular legalization is added. For a non-Hague destination only, consular legalization before that destination's consulate may be used as the exclusive alternative; the two paths are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Current Standing of the Hong Kong parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: Hong Kong Companies Registry issues the certificate, and the High Court of Hong Kong Apostille Section affixes the apostille. No consular legalization is added. If the receiving state is not an Apostille Convention member, use consular legalization solely; do not sequence apostille and consular legalization together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing WFOE formation, name clearance, and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong parent, notarized by a Hong Kong notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: notarization of signatures by a Hong Kong notary public, then apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong Apostille Section. No consular legalization is added. For non-Hague destinations, replace the apostille step with consular legalization by the destination consulate; never apply both mechanisms.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Hong Kong parent (certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: certified copy issued by the Hong Kong Companies Registry, then apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong Apostille Section. No consular legalization is added. For non-Hague Convention states, consular legalization is the parallel and exclusive substitute; do not chain it with an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Financial Standing Letter for the Hong Kong parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: bank officer signing authority is notarized by a Hong Kong notary public, then the High Court of Hong Kong Apostille Section affixes an apostille. No consular legalization is added. If the destination is a non-Hague state, consular legalization alone is required; apostille and consular legalization are never sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct risk-based enhanced due diligence on all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, and every UBO owning 25% or more of the WFOE or the Hong Kong parent. Screen continuously against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, PBOC and Ministry of Public Security terrorist designation lists, and domestic PEP registers, with adverse-media and negative-news monitoring. Require source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for each individual UBO, and impose mandatory board-level sign-off for any PEP, family member, close associate, or sanctioned entity. Re-screen every 24 hours and upon any ownership or control change; retain CDD and UBO records for at least five years after the relationship ends, compliant with PBOC Order No. 3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Self-Declaration and Registration Online Platform, operated through provincial and municipal market regulation bureaus
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in simplified Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier naming convention: Administrative Division + Distinctive Trade Name + Industry or Business Organization Characteristics + Limited Liability Company. The English name is a non-statutory translation and must use pinyin transliteration consistently in bank, tax, customs, and UBO filings. A separate English-only statutory name is not permitted, and names containing provincial or national administrative features are subject to special SAMR review.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, submit a written administrative review application within 15 working days to the same market regulation bureau that issued the rejection, including the rejection notice, the proposed Chinese name with pinyin transliteration, the four-tier naming breakdown, and evidence of distinctiveness. If the bureau upholds the rejection, file an administrative reconsideration application with the provincial SAMR or the central SAMR within 60 days of the rejection decision, and attach all prior decisions. A direct administrative lawsuit before a competent People's Court may be filed within six months without exhausting reconsideration, but reconsideration is recommended for speed. Include at least three alternative names in the appeal to preserve the WFOE formation timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox arrangements are not permissible for this WFOE. The business under ISIC 3250 / NAICS 334510 is the manufacture of portable phased-array medical diagnostic scanners (color Doppler ultrasound consoles) for export, which requires a physical production site, registered lease, installed equipment, on-site employees, actual inventory movement, and customs/tax substance. SAMR registration, the medical products administration (NMPA), municipal tax authorities, customs, and commercial banks uniformly reject a virtual address for this industry and will classify the entity as high-risk for false commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk, quantified at 80-90% within the first 24 months after incorporation. Checklist: unannounced SAMR verification of the registered office and production site; NMPA on-site inspection of the quality management system for medical device production license; municipal tax field inspection for actual employees, rent invoices, and utility bills; customs export audit of physical warehouse and goods movement; verification of lease contracts, floor plans, production machinery, inventory records, and staff interviews. Failure results in business license revocation, administrative fines, customs export sanctions, and mandatory re-inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2023), Articles 4, 9, 23-36, 46-50; Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration; enterprise establishment registration window
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company together with the Articles of Association, legal representative appointment letter, and foreign investment negative list compliance declaration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None at general statutory level; the registered capital is self-declared in the Articles of Association and must be subscribed by the Hong Kong sole shareholder. There is no statutory blocked escrow account requirement for a general manufacturing WFOE, but the capital contribution schedule must be documented in the corporate records and may be verified by the company's auditor, banking counterparties, and foreign exchange authorities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LTD (THE COMPANY) ADOPTED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANY LAW OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF CHINA, THE FOREIGN INVESTMENT LAW, AND THE ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION. RESOLVED, that the Company shall be formed as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise with the name and registered office approved in the Articles of Association. RESOLVED, that the Board acknowledges the subscription by the sole shareholder, the Hong Kong parent entity, to the entire registered capital of RMB [amount], and directs the legal representative to cause the capital contribution schedule and all equity interests to be recorded in the Company's books and statutory registers, and to make all filings with the State Administration for Market Regulation and the competent foreign investment information reporting system. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be [address], and that the Chief Executive Officer or legal representative is authorized to execute lease agreements, landlord certificates, and municipal registration documents necessary to evidence the registered office. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open bank accounts, including a basic deposit account, a RMB capital contribution account, and, if required, a foreign exchange capital account, and that the authorized signatories named in the board resolution, two of whom must act jointly, are authorized to execute account opening documents, online banking mandates, tax payment instructions, and treasury operations in accordance with anti-money laundering and know-your-customer procedures. RESOLVED, that [name 1] is appointed as chairman and legal representative, [name 2] as director and general manager, and [name 3] as supervisor, and that the legal representative is authorized to apply for corporate seals, business licenses, tax registration, and to open payroll and settlement accounts. RESOLVED, that the Board authorizes and directs the general manager to retain, at corporate expense, counsel, accountants, and consultants, and to prepare, sign, and file all applications for medical device product registration, production license, environmental impact assessment, fire protection approvals, and any other regulatory permits necessary for the manufacture of the color Doppler ultrasound console. RESOLVED, that any officer or director acting pursuant to these resolutions may take all lawful actions reasonably required to implement the intent of this resolution, and that such actions shall be ratified and confirmed as within the authority granted. RESOLVED, that these resolutions take immediate effect upon signature and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name pre-approval and foreign investment negative list screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation online enterprise name reservation platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the State Administration for Market Regulation online name reservation service to verify the proposed Chinese and English trade name against nationwide databases, and screen the project against the Foreign Investment Negative List. The Hong Kong parent company must submit a notarized certificate of incorporation and a certificate of good standing issued by the Hong Kong Companies Registry. The authorized officer shall upload the power of attorney and personal identification, select the preferred company form as a limited liability company, and reserve the name for six months. After approval, the name reservation notice will be issued and must be used in the subsequent establishment application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name or names
Hong Kong parent company certificate of incorporation
Certificate of good standing from Hong Kong Companies Registry
Notarized power of attorney in favor of the authorized representative
Passport or corporate authorization of the designated filing officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is queried due to similarity, the authorized officer shall submit alternative name choices and request an expedited manual review. If the negative list screening raises a restricted industry issue, the WFOE structure must be revised or approval from the competent commerce authority must be obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application and issuance of business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration government service hall or provincial online government service platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company, the Articles of Association, the name reservation notice, office lease and title certificates, shareholder credentials, and appointment documents for the legal representative, directors, and supervisor to the Local Market Supervision Administration. The authority will review the company name, registered capital, business scope, legal representative disqualification, and compliance with the foreign investment negative list. After approval, the SAMR issues the business license with a unified social credit code and the establishment filing is synchronized to the taxation and statistics systems. The WFOE obtains legal personality on the date of license issuance.
required_dossiers: Business name reservation notice
Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company
Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder
Lease agreement and landlord title certificate for the registered office
Notarized certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of the Hong Kong parent
Legal representative, director, and supervisor identification documents
Letter of appointment or sole shareholder resolution
Foreign Investment Negative List compliance declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SAMR issues a rectification notice, the company must respond within 30 days by amending the Articles of Association or supplementary filings. If the business scope or company name is rejected, the filing officer shall revise and resubmit through the online platform and request accelerated re-review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation registrations including corporate seal, tax, social insurance, and foreign investment reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau approved seal engraving service; State Taxation Administration local branch; Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Ministry of Commerce foreign investment information reporting system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after the issuance of the business license, the legal representative must apply for public security bureau approved corporate seals, including the company seal, finance seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal. The company must register with the local tax authority for tax identification, select taxpayer status and invoice type, complete social insurance registration at the human resources and social security bureau, and open a basic deposit account. The WFOE must also complete the Foreign Investment Information Reporting on the Ministry of Commerce online reporting system. Each agency will issue registration certificates or confirmation notices, and the completed files must be kept in the corporate statutory record book.
required_dossiers: Business license original and duplicate
Legal representative identity document
Corporate seal and finance seal application form
Tax registration and taxpayer status forms
Social insurance registration form
Foreign Investment Information Report receipt or online reference number
Basic deposit account opening confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration fails due to data mismatch, coordinate with the SAMR to correct the unified social credit code and tax files and resubmit. If social insurance registration is suspended, cure by submitting the missing employment or address declarations and satisfy any outstanding fine before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign exchange registration, capital injection, and bank account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange through a designated domestic bank with foreign exchange business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The WFOE must complete foreign exchange registration for the foreign-invested enterprise through its chosen domestic bank, for the establishment of the foreign exchange capital account needed for the Hong Kong parent company's capital injection. The Hong Kong shareholder shall transfer the subscribed capital by wire transfer or SWIFT in accordance with the approved contribution schedule. The bank will conduct a client due diligence review and may require the company to provide source of funds evidence and the board resolution approving the capital injection. Once the capital is received, the bank shall issue a foreign exchange registration confirmation and the company shall record the contribution in its capital verification records.
required_dossiers: Business license
Foreign Investment Information Reporting completion certificate
Foreign exchange registration form for foreign-invested enterprises
Bank account opening documents and KYC forms
Board-approved capital contribution schedule
Source of funds evidence from the Hong Kong parent
Power of attorney for bank account signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC or anti-money laundering documents, the legal representative shall supply the renewed business license, audited parent financial statements, and a full corporate ownership chart within 10 working days. If SAFE registration is rejected, correct the foreign investment information report and resubmit with the discrepancy explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory record book completion and handover to industrial licensing phase
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration; legal counsel coordinating the NMPA industrial licensing work stream
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once all post-incorporation registrations are complete, the company must maintain a statutory corporate record book containing the business license, Articles of Association, board resolutions, shareholder register, capital contribution records, foreign investment information reporting certificate, seal card, and authority matrix. The legal representative must file any changes in directors, supervisors, or registered address within 15 days with the SAMR. This step closes the statutory incorporation task and converts the dossier to the industrial licensing phase for the National Medical Products Administration medical device registration, production license, environmental impact assessment, and fire safety permits.
required_dossiers: Business license
Articles of Association
Board resolutions and shareholder register
Capital contribution records and bank receipts
Foreign investment information reporting certificate
Seal card and authorized signatory list
Change or amendment filings if any corporate details were updated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SAMR queries the statutory record book or filings, submit the missing corporate records within 15 days. If beneficial ownership information is requested, provide the updated shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner table and re-file the annual report or change notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) and provincial Medical Products Administration; quality management system audit under NMPA medical device good manufacturing practice requirements
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Production License and Medical Device Registration Certificate for the Color Doppler Ultrasound Diagnostic Console

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and provincial-level Ecology and Environment Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category-based classification under the MEE Classification List of Construction Projects for Environmental Impact Assessment. Assembly-only medical electronic device manufacturing is generally eligible for Environmental Impact Registration Form filing, while facilities involving soldering, chemical etching, plating, coating, or hazardous waste-generating processes are subject to a full Environmental Impact Report Form and technical review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to a municipal sewage system must meet pH 6-9, COD not exceeding 500 mg/L, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, and SS not exceeding 400 mg/L under GB8978-1996 integrated wastewater discharge standard unless stricter local standards apply. VOCs emitted from any surface coating or solvent use must comply with GB16297-1996, with non-methane total hydrocarbons not exceeding 120 mg/m3 at the treatment outlet. Hazardous waste must be stored in compliance with GB18597-2023 and consigned to a licensed disposal company within 90 days. If ethylene oxide sterilization is used, workplace exposure limits under GBZ2.1 and area exhaust treatment standards must be observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety acceptance or archival filing with the local Fire and Rescue Brigade under GB50016, including fire prevention inspection certificate for the production and warehousing zones, emergency evacuation plan approval, and fire extinguishing system inspection. The facility must also obtain a structural load inspection certificate if installing heavy imaging assembly fixtures or shielded test enclosures, and workplace safety approval from the local Emergency Management Bureau covering occupational health, machine guarding, electrical safety, and chemical storage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); local district/county tax services; online portal: the STA Electronic Tax Bureau (E-Tax Bureau / Electronic Taxpayer Service Platform). For customs and foreign-exchange clearance, the China Customs Single Window and SAFE reporting are integrated with STA data.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) with the Administration for Market Regulation and obtain the Business License bearing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). Step 2: The USCC is automatically transmitted to the tax authority through the national 'one-license-one-code' information sharing system; the WFOE is tax-registered and the USCC serves as the legal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT taxpayer number. Step 3: Activate the E-Tax Bureau account, complete the taxpayer registration confirmation, record the legal representative, financial/accounting software, bank settlement account, contact information, and entity-level ownership details. Step 4: Apply for VAT General Taxpayer status if annual taxable sales will exceed RMB 5,000,000 or voluntarily if the statutory conditions are met. Step 5: Register for Full Digital Electronic Invoice capability and obtain any remaining tax-control/issuance facilities required for the taxpayer's invoicing category. Step 6: For a foreign non-resident corporate shareholder (including the Hong Kong parent), no separate Chinese TIN is required for passive holding income; where China-sourced income arises, the non-resident registers through the WFOE's withholding declarations in the E-Tax Bureau and may, where applicable, claim treaty benefits under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA upon presenting a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC enterprise income tax system does not contain a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. A resident WFOE is a separate entity-level taxpayer on worldwide income; no pass-through eligibility exists for Chinese limited companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) administered by the State Taxation Administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (annual taxable turnover excluding VAT). Exceeding this amount during any continuous 12-month rolling period mandates VAT General Taxpayer registration; below this amount the WFOE may remain a Small-Scale Taxpayer unless it voluntarily elects General Taxpayer status. Regardless of turnover, every entity must complete tax registration within 30 days after the business license is issued.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates nationwide real-time invoice clearance through the STA E-Tax Bureau and the Golden Tax Phase IV system. Full Digital Electronic Invoices (FDEI) are issued, number-stamped, encrypted and transmitted in real time through the STA electronic invoice platform; no artificial stamps are added after issuance. VAT Special Invoices must be verified and authenticated before the input tax credit can be recognized. Third-party SaaS invoicing tools must connect through STA-certified API interfaces. The invoice unique code and anti-counterfeit digital stamp operate as the fiscal seal; duplicate or backdated invoicing is blocked by the central tax database. For export sales, the e-invoice and export customs declaration data are matched automatically with the export tax refund declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A WFOE manufacturing and exporting Color Doppler ultrasound consoles qualifies for the input-credit-refund export model for production enterprises and the export VAT zero-rating/exemption if it is a VAT General Taxpayer, the goods are physically exported from mainland China to an overseas customs territory (including Hong Kong SAR), the China Customs export declaration is issued in the exporter's name, the sales are accurately invoiced and declared in the E-Tax Bureau, the foreign currency proceeds are repatriated to China through an approved bank within 180 days (or a valid delay/dispensation is filed), and the export does not distort the underlying business purpose. Qualifying offshore digital services are not within this scope.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Declaration (export goods declaration form) with actual clearance endorsement via the China Customs Single Window
Commercial invoice, packing list and sales contract/purchase order
Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air), or road/rail cross-border transport manifest endorsed by China Customs evidencing physical export to Hong Kong SAR or other destination
VAT Special Invoice or equivalent input-tax documentation for purchased materials and processing costs
Bank Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance Confirmation/Export Proceeds Receipt Certificate (SAFE-standard bank receipt) evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Export Tax Refund/Exemption Declaration Form submitted through the E-Tax Bureau, with the export rebate declaration data set matched to customs and banking records
Medical device export compliance documents (Medical Device Registration Certificate and Export Sales Confirmation) where required by the National Medical Products Administration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and customs joint audit system verifies export declarations, logistics waybills, bank receipts, e-invoice data and tax refund claims. If zero-rating is claimed without proof of physical export, without timely foreign exchange repatriation, or with false or inconsistent documentation, the export tax refund and exempted output VAT are clawed back with late-payment surcharge (0.05% per day on overdue tax). For fraudulent export refunds, the enterprise must repay the amounts refunded and may be fined from one to five times the tax involved; the tax authority may suspend all future export tax rebate services and transfer the case for criminal prosecution (crime of fraudulent export tax refund) where imprisonment and criminal fines apply. The statutory limitation for retrospective clawback is five years; in cases of fraud involving the public tax fund, recovery is pursued without a limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBoC), with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the separate central monetary authority for the Hong Kong SAR clearing hub.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China operates a managed current-account convertibility regime administered by SAFE. Trade-related foreign exchange receipts and payments are permitted through designated banks after verification of customs declarations, sales contracts, invoices, and shipping documentation. Capital-account flows, including equity subscriptions by the Hong Kong parent, intercompany loans, debt financing, and profit repatriation, are not freely convertible and require prior SAFE registration, a valid FDI filing, and a licensed bank's compliance judgment before funds are credited or disbursed. Hong Kong SAR, by contrast, maintains full convertibility under the Common Law framework and the HKMA's Linked Exchange Rate system, with no surrender requirements for HKD, USD, or other major currencies. For the mainland WFOE, the most demanding hurdle is outward remittance of profits to the Hong Kong shareholder: the bank will require audited financial statements, completed withholding tax settlement at the treaty-reduced rate under the mainland-HK double tax arrangement, a board resolution approving the dividend, an SAFE profit repatriation filing, and proof that the capital account has been used only for the approved business scope. Current-account trade settlements remain practical for procurement of ultrasound console components and export proceeds, but equity injections, dividends, and any capital-account movement remain documentary and compliance-intensive.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's current-account rules for goods trade, export foreign currency proceeds must be repatriated into China and credited to the WFOE's trade foreign exchange income account within 90 days of the customs export declaration. There is no statutory mandatory surrender ratio; the enterprise may retain USD, HKD, EUR, or other earned currencies in its settlement account or voluntarily convert them into RMB onshore at prevailing market rates. If payment is expected after the 90-day collection window, or if advance export proceeds have been received more than 90 days before the shipment will be exported, the WFOE must file a delayed collection or advance receipt report in the SAFE trade-monitoring system before the bank executes the transaction. Failure to report creates a compliance flag and may suspend the entity's A-class trade foreign exchange status.

Capital Account for Foreign Investment and RMB Basic Deposit Account for operating expenses
Hong Kong treasury concentration account for HKD/USD liquidity and trade finance issuance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Not viable for the mainland WFOE. PBoC and SAFE regulations restrict domestic CNY account opening and FX settlement to commercial banks and licensed non-bank payment institutions; no offshore fintech EMI legal wrapper is recognised by Chinese banking law as an authorised depository for FDI capital, export proceeds, or SAFE-registered payments. An offshore EMI could theoretically support the Hong Kong treasury vehicle's non-mainland operational cash flows, but it still requires an underlying Hong Kong bank account and cannot be used to book mainland FX settlements, perform capital verification, or satisfy export-import matching. Therefore, all capital injections, trade disbursements, and FX hedging for this medical-device exporter must be routed through a mainland Tier-1 licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative and at least one authorised signatory of the WFOE must physically appear at the mainland branch for initial onboarding. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted by Chinese Tier-1 banks for a newly formed WFOE with foreign shareholders. The bank will conduct a face-to-face interview, verify original passports and corporate formation instruments, and witness signatures on the account-opening agreement. For the Hong Kong treasury arm, HKMA-licensed banks may permit a video interview plus notarised corporate documents after the beneficial ownership structure has been confirmed, but full physical presence of a director remains the most conservative and reliable underwriting posture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blurred ultimate beneficial ownership across the Hong Kong parent and the mainland WFOE, particularly if shares are held through a Hong Kong nominee or a non-operating investment holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart, certificates of incorporation for each legal entity layer, register of directors and shareholders, valid passports of all individuals owning or controlling 10 percent or more of the WFOE, stamped trust deed or nominee agreement, audited financial statements of the holding entity, and a written source-of-wealth statement explaining the origin of the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export of portable phased-array medical ultrasound consoles with embedded software and electronic sub-components potentially triggers dual-use, sanctions, or medical-device export-control reviews by the bank's compliance committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NMPA medical device registration certificate for each commercial model, CE or FDA registration for target markets, free sale certificate issued by the competent health authority, ECCN and HTS classification with a customs broker advisory opinion, internal OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening report showing no adverse hits, and end-user/end-use certificates signed by the overseas distributor or hospital network.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators arising from high invoice unit prices for color Doppler ultrasound systems, bill-to/ship-to mismatches, or a third-party payment from an entity not named as buyer in the underlying export contract.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original signed sales contract, proforma invoice and final commercial invoice, customs export declaration, bill of lading or air waybill, packing list, independent third-party inspection certificate, marine or cargo insurance certificate, and a written explanation of any logistics intermediary payment arrangement including the correspondent bank details and the ultimate beneficiary confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious rapid circular flows between the Hong Kong treasury account and the mainland WFOE's capital account, suggesting unregistered intra-group lending or round-tripping of investment funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE foreign direct investment registration certificate, bank credit records for each capital payment matched to a statutory audited capital verification report issued by a licensed PRC certified public accountant, board minutes authorising the transfer, a signed intercompany loan agreement if any debt capital is used, and a deployment schedule showing that funds are applied only to tangible operating assets, raw materials, payroll, and export settlements within the WFOE's approved business scope.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong parent shall transmit FDI capital via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital settlement account at a mainland Tier-1 bank. The remittance instruction must cite the SAFE FDI registration number and the payment purpose code attributable to foreign direct investment capital injection. The receiving bank will place the credit into the capital settlement account pending verification. A licensed PRC certified public accountant must then issue an audited capital verification report before the capital can be converted into RMB and transferred into the general operating account. Subsequent disbursements must respect the foreign investment negative list for medical device manufacturing and cannot be deployed into securities, entrusted loans, non-operating real estate, or speculative financial products. If urgent trade payments arise, the WFOE may apply under the SAFE capital-account settlement convenience pilot, provided the full audit trail and internal governance structure remain intact.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For export sales of color Doppler ultrasound consoles, the preferred clearing rail is a sight or usance commercial letter of credit issued by the buyer's bank and advised through the WFOE's mainland bank; SWIFT MT700 and MT707 messages govern LC issuance, amendments, and documentary compliance. For smaller distributors and after-sales service parts, the WFOE may accept SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers, but each payment must be supported by a signed sale contract, commercial invoice, transport document, packing list, certificate of origin, and inspection certificate. Documentary collections such as D/P and D/A are permissible only for low-risk repeat buyers in non-sanctioned jurisdictions and must be routed through the same advising bank to preserve continuity of the audit trail. HKD/USD clearing between the Hong Kong treasury vehicle and the mainland WFOE will be executed via SWIFT and the Hong Kong CHATS system; domestic CNY payments between the WFOE and local suppliers will clear over CIPS or through commercial bank interbank settlement networks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD trade-backed forward contracts offered by the mainland settlement bank under SAFE current-account registration, with tenors limited to the maturity of the underlying export receivable and no speculative rollover.
Onshore CNY/HKD FX swap contracts for managing timing mismatches between HKD capital inflows and CNY operating expenses, supported by genuine trade or dividend cash-flow exposure.

Cross-currency interest rate swap on long-term foreign-currency debt only when the loan is SAFE-registered, the notional is capped at outstanding debt, and the contract hedges actual coupon or principal repayment obligations.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) in CNH is permissible only through the Hong Kong treasury vehicle and may not be booked inside the mainland WFOE; it may hedge CNH exposure arising from intercompany royalties or cross-border services subject to HKMA market conduct standards and underlying exposure documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) for a private company limited by shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of incorporation (the return date) each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late delivery triggers an additional fee of HKD 870 if filed within 3 months after the return date, HKD 1,740 if filed within 3 to 6 months, and HKD 3,480 if filed more than 6 months late. Offences attract fines up to HKD 50,000 plus HKD 1,000 per day of continued default. Persistent non-filing for more than 12 months can lead to administrative strike-off and dissolution under section 746 of the Companies Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the expiry date of the current business registration certificate, or within 1 month from the date of demand if the renewal notice is issued by the IRD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew is an offence under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310, s.12) punishable by a fine of up to HKD 5,000 and imprisonment for up to 1 year, plus a daily fine of HKD 50 for continued unregistered operation. Continued default permits the IRD to certify the business as inactive, enabling the Companies Registry to initiate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) together with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Profits Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the date of issue of the return notice by the IRD; for a 31 December accounting period, the notice is generally issued on 1 April and filed by 1 May for paper filing, with extended deadlines allowed for e-filing by an authorised tax representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the company and responsible persons to prosecution under section 80(3) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance with fines up to HKD 10,000, additional tax up to 10% of the undercharged tax, and on conviction fines up to three times the tax under-assessed. The IRD may also raise estimated assessments, causing a 5% surcharge and statutory interest on unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A and BIR56B) for staff remuneration for the year of assessment ended 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the issue date of the return notice, normally 1 April each year, unless an online filing extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A failure without reasonable excuse is an offence punishable by a fine of up to HKD 10,000 and, if the failure persists, additional tax up to 10% of the tax undercharged plus prosecution before the District Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and laying of audited financial statements and reports before members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members of the company; compliance supervised by the Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the end of the accounting reference period, unless dispensed with by unanimous written resolution in a private company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention is an offence for the company and every responsible officer, with fines and daily default fines under the Companies Ordinance; repeated non-compliance can be treated as a ground for administrative strike-off by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under sections 394 and 403 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every Hong Kong incorporated company is required to appoint a certified public accountant firm as auditor and to have its financial statements audited annually. There are no turnover, balance-sheet, or headcount thresholds that exempt an ordinary private company from this audit obligation. The only quantitative legal thresholds relevant to financial reporting are the simplified reporting criteria for small private companies under Part 9 of Cap. 622: a company qualifies as small if it satisfies at least two of the following three conditions in the financial year: annual revenue not exceeding HKD 20 million, total assets not exceeding HKD 10 million, and not more than 50 employees. Qualifying small private companies may prepare simplified financial statements, but those statements remain subject to a mandatory statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are fully converged with IFRS, or with HKFRS for Private Companies where the company is eligible; the audit is performed in accordance with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing (HKSA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require an annual UBO filing with the Companies Registry. Instead, the company must maintain a Register of Significant Controllers (ROS) at its registered office under Part 17A of the Companies Ordinance. The ROS must be updated within 7 days of the company becoming aware of any change in significant controller particulars or receiving a notice from the controller. For share transfers, the Register of Members must be updated promptly upon lodgement of the transfer; the next annual return (NAR1) filed within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation reflects the register of members as at the return date, including transfers registered within the preceding 30-day window. Changes in directors and company secretary must be separately notified to the Companies Registry within 15 days, and allotments of shares must be reported on Form NSC1 within 1 month of allotment. ROS records must be retained for at least 6 years after an individual ceases to be a significant controller.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Company Secretary
Register of Charges and copies of instruments creating charges
Minutes of General Meetings and Board Meetings including written resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Applicable PRC Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) incentives include: 15% preferential rate for certified High-and-New-Technology Enterprises (HNTE); effective 5% rate for qualifying small-or-low-profit enterprises (SLPE) with taxable income within RMB 3 million and revenue/asset thresholds; 100% additional R&D expense super-deduction for qualifying manufacturing R&D on medical imaging equipment; potential free-trade-zone preferential treatment for certain encouraged high-tech sectors; and 10-year loss carryforward for HNTE and technology-oriented advanced-service enterprises whereas the general carryforward is 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Form A100000 Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (Class A) plus supporting schedules A101010/A102010, A105000, A106000, A107012, A107040, A108010 and transfer-pricing schedules; e-filed through the Chinese Taxpayer Electronic Tax Bureau (eTax portal / Golden Tax IV) at the corporate municipality's competent state tax office. Quarterly interim prepayment returns are filed on Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final reconciliation; quarterly interim prepayment declarations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The fiscal year is 1 January to 31 December. Quarterly prepayment is due within 15 calendar days after the end of each quarter. The annual EIT return and audited supporting schedules are due on or before 31 May of the following year. Dividend withholding tax must be declared and remitted to the tax bureau by the WFOE acting as withholding agent on the payment date of the dividend; for treaty-rate claims, the administrative application for reduced withholding must be completed before or at the time of the remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue (营业收入) from sales of color Doppler ultrasound consoles and related medical-device parts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record all revenue from domestic and export sales of ISIC 3250 color Doppler ultrasound console units. Revenue booked to a Hong Kong related purchaser must be at arm's length; if the WFOE sells finished consoles to the HK affiliate below manufacturing cost or at a margin that does not reflect the WFOE's production,distribution and licensing functions, the tax authority will make a special tax adjustment. Accrual method applies; no revenue offset against intercompany receivables.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs (营业成本) including raw materials, components, factory labor, depreciation of production equipment, and subcontracted processing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Import costs for transducers, phased-array probes, semiconductor components and software licenses bought from the HK parent or other related suppliers must be supported by customs documentation, invoices and transfer-pricing analyses. Related-party purchase prices must satisfy the arm's-length standard. Inflating the cost base by paying excessive import prices to a Hong Kong intermediary will trigger transfer-pricing audit and may be penalized as tax evasion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges (税金及附加) excluding income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include consumption tax where applicable, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duties and property-related taxes. Do not deduct EIT prepayments, late-payment surcharges, penalties, foreign taxes imposed on the Hong Kong shareholder, or dividend withholding taxes borne by the WFOE on behalf of the foreign parent; such items are nondeductible and must be added back in the special tax adjustment schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, administrative expenses and financial expenses (销售费用、管理费用、财务费用).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees or headquarters (including cross-charges from the Hong Kong holding company) are deductible only if the service was actually rendered, there is demonstrable benefit to the WFOE, the fee is arm's length, and no duplicate reimbursement occurs. Validate related-party service invoices, staff time records and cost-allocation keys. Thin-capitalization rules apply: shareholder loans generally within a 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial enterprises, with interest exceeding arm's-length rates or the statutory ratio not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit and total accounting profit before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reconcile with the PRC statutory financial statements. Non-operating income includes government grants, foreign-exchange gains, penalties recovered and dividends from foreign subsidiaries. Dividends received by the WFOE from a Hong Kong affiliate are generally taxable as worldwide income of a Chinese tax-resident enterprise; a foreign tax credit may apply for HK tax suffered if the income is not treaty-exempt or not eligible for China's participation exemption rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment increases (纳税调增) and decreases (纳税调减).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible payments to the Hong Kong parent: non-beneficial service charges, excessive royalties or license fees for ultrasound software, entertainment expenses exceeding the statutory percentage, unpaid withholding taxes borne by the WFOE, interest in excess of thin-cap limits, and any transfer-pricing adjustment under special tax collection. Subtract qualifying R&D super deductions, tax-exempt income and losses compensated by after-tax reserves. Cross-border payments to an intermediary in a no-treaty jurisdiction must be scrutinized under the,substance-over-form doctrine.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate application, tax amount and tax reductions/credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory 25% rate to taxable income. If HNTE certification is obtained, apply 15%; if the enterprise qualifies as a small-or-low-profit enterprise, apply the effective 5% concessionary rate. Legislative and incentive schedules must be documented. Reduction or exemption amounts must be substantiated by HNTE certificate or software/medical-device encouraged-industry documentation; no treaty credit is available to reduce the WFOE's mainland EIT for HK withholding solely on distributed profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 23 / Box 24 / Box 25 / Box 26 / Box 27 / Box 28
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final EIT liability, foreign tax credit, quarterly prepayments already made, and amount of tax due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the final computation after offsetting current-year and prior-year prepayments. Foreign tax credits for income earned in Hong Kong or other jurisdictions are limited to the PRC EIT payable on that foreign-source income. No credit is allowed for the Hong Kong withholding tax that the HK parent would suffer when profits are declared at the HK level. The resulting tax due is payable upon filing; refunds are credited after tax bureau verification. When declaring a dividend to the HK parent, the WFOE must withhold PRC dividend WHT and separately file the non-resident withholding return (withholding agent return), applying the treaty-reduced rate only after statutory procedural formalities are completed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual EIT filing: tax authorities may order correction and impose a fine of RMB 2,000 for ordinary cases and up to RMB 50,000 for serious cases under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) Article 62. Late payment or underpayment of EIT: daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under TCAL Article 32. Tax evasion through false receipts, false revenue, inflated intercompany costs or sham Hong Kong arrangements: additional tax plus a penalty of 50% to five times the evaded tax under TCAL Article 63. Failure by a withholding agent to withhold dividend, interest or royalty WHT: penalty of 50% to 300% of the unwithheld amount under TCAL Article 69. Criminal tax fraud or tax evasion under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 may subject the entity to fines and the responsible directors and finance executives to imprisonment of up to seven years for substantial evasion, with travel restrictions and the taxation administration's serious-untrustworthy-taxpayer blacklisting.
